statement: In a club, 4 children play chess. That is a quarter of all the children in the club. How many children are in the club?

choices.misconception: I shared the 4 children into 4 equal parts.
I gave the number of children who play chess, not the whole club.
I doubled 4, as if a quarter were a half.
I counted only the children who do not play chess.

hints: A quarter is one of how many equal parts?
A quarter means the whole club is split into 4 equal groups, and the chess players fill one of them. Build the whole club from 4 groups that size.
One quarter is 4 children, so each of the 4 equal groups has 4 children.

solutions.reliable: A quarter is one of 4 equal parts. One part is 4 children, so the whole club is 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 = 16 children. Check: a quarter of 16 is 4. The idea to keep: if you know one equal part, build the whole by putting all the parts back together.
solutions.elegant: Half the club is twice a quarter, 8 children, and the whole club is twice that, 16.

whyOnTest: Going from a part back to the whole checks real understanding of a quarter, not just dividing by 4.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
